events.text: At {wd_inn} three tithe-collectors of a jealous hill-god have the old host cornered against the lamp-rack over an unpaid lamp-tithe. The pilgrims study their sandals. The host, ash to the elbows, looks straight at you, the only stranger who walked in with a plain mask on.

effects.log: You stand, and the mask does not slip, but the room feels you. The collectors weigh their chances and decide the tithe can wait a season. The host presses a lit lamp into your hands.
You do not ask them to stop. A bench breaks, the collectors go down the steps, and every shrine on the road whispers of a masked stranger.

choices.text: Keep your eyes on your sandals

effects.log: It is not a shrine you serve and not a quarrel of yours. The collectors take the lamp-oil and go, and the host does not look at you again.

events.text: A cart of offerings has gone over at the gate of {wd_inn}: rice cakes in the mud, candles rolling, a mule screaming in the traces and a pilgrim's child pinned under the wheel. The yard is full of worshippers. None of them moves.

effects.log: You set your shoulder to it and heave. The child crawls free. The pilgrim will not stop thanking a stranger, and the whole house sets a lamp for you.
You call six worshippers to the wheel together. It works. They are a little proud afterwards, and so are you.
Someone else lifts it eventually. You are already back on the road.

events.text: The collectors bullying the host of {wd_inn} look at you and go very quiet. Your mask is thin, and a god's weight does not hide well in a small shrine. The leader lays the lamp-oil on the altar with both hands.

choices.text: Let them go with a warning

effects.log: They go, bowing to the mask. The host pours you tea with shaking hands and refuses your thanks.
You make an example. Whole hill-shrines will talk of it for a month, and the jealous god will hear.

events.text: A donor in temple silks at {wd_inn} is scolding a young shrine-boy for knocking over a votive lamp. The room has gone quiet. The donor notices your look, laughs, and says something about knowing a servant's place before the gods.

choices.text: Relight the lamp with a breath and shame the donor

effects.log: The lamp wakes at your breath, and the donor, who felt something old pass by, suddenly finds a pressing errand outside.
The flame takes. The scolding stops, if only because the donor is confused.
The donor pours you a cup of offering-tea. It tastes of nothing.

events.text: {npc} sits down across from you at {wd_inn} without asking, because every other bench is full, and orders two bowls of offering-rice instead of one. "You look like someone who has walked a long way in a borrowed face," {he} says. "So have I. Eat."

mem.note: shared a table and a long night of stories

effects.log: By the second pot you have each told the other things you have told nobody. {npc} laughs like a temple door flung open.
{npc} does not mind. At dawn {he} pays for both bowls and is gone, leaving a note: "Same road, maybe."
{npc} shrugs and takes the rice to the steps.

events.text: A storm keeps the pilgrims indoors at {wd_inn} for three days, and on the second you and {npc}, a traveller with a cracked prayer-drum, start a game of twelve domains with painted tiles by the hearth. By the third day the whole shrine is watching, and neither of you has won a round.

effects.log: {npc} knows you let {him} win, and likes you better for it.

mem.note: lost a good game to you

effects.log: You win by a single tile. {npc} stares at the board, then laughs and demands another.

events.text: {npc} looks up when you come into {wd_inn}, and stares. "The old pilgrims told of a god who walked masked, called {wd_past_title}," {he} says. "You walk the way they said. Forgive me. Sit, please. I am buying." Something in you, older than this mask, turns over in its sleep.

effects.log: The stories are wrong in every detail and right in every way that matters. {npc} tells them with shining eyes.

choices.text: Say you have never heard the name

effects.log: {npc} looks disappointed, then sly. "Of course not," {he} says, and buys you a bowl anyway.

events.text: {npc}, a skinny young pilgrim with a reed for a staff, has been watching you eat at {wd_inn} for an hour. At last {he} comes over and kneels on the flagstones. "Let me carry your lamp," {he} says. "Or teach me. I do not care which. I only want to go where you are going."

effects.log: You tell {npc} to get up off the flagstones. {He} follows you out into the morning, grinning.

mem.note: was given advice and a blessing

effects.log: You tell {npc} which shrines keep honest priests and give {him} a small blessing for the road.
"Go home," you say. {npc} goes, slowly, looking back.

events.text: {npc} is sweeping the steps of {wd_inn} for a bowl of rice, and has been watching you since you came in. When you stand to go, {he} drops the broom. "I have heard of your pantheon," {he} says. "Everyone on this road has. Is it true it takes anyone who will serve?"

effects.log: You bring {npc} home. The temple guards look at the broom-callused hands and nod.

choices.text: Tell {him} the truth about the service

effects.log: You tell {npc} how hard it is. {He} listens to every word and is still there in the morning.

mem.note: was told there was no room

effects.log: {npc} picks the broom back up.

events.text: Two young novices are quarrelling over the last offering cake at {wd_inn}, and the smaller one, {npc}, is winning, which is interesting. When it is over, {npc} gives the cake back to the bigger one. You watch {him} do it, and think of your own shrine, and your own halls with room in them.

choices.text: Offer {npc} a place at your shrine

mem.note: was offered a place at your shrine

effects.log: {npc} stares, then bows so low {his} forehead hits the floor. You have a new acolyte, found on the road.
You set a whole tray of cakes before them. Both novices remember you for years.

events.text: At {wd_inn} the cantors are practising, and {npc} is the one flat note in the choir. A cantor glares; {npc} only shrugs, finds your eye across the hall, and beams. After the rite {he} crosses to you. "You were smiling at my flat note," {he} says. "Confess."

mem.note: talked until the lamps burned low

effects.log: "Then you have no ear," {npc} says, sitting down, "and I like you anyway." You talk until the lamps burn low.
{npc} looks at you a long moment, then laughs. "Good answer," {he} says.
{npc} shrugs, and starts another hymn.

events.text: The only seat left at {wd_inn} is beside {npc}, who has a map of the twelve domains spread over half the table and is arguing with it. "This road does not exist," {npc} says to you, as if you had been sitting there for hours. "I have walked it twice."

effects.log: You redraw the road together on the back of the offering list. {npc} keeps the list.
You trade roads until midnight. {npc} has walked farther than you, and listened better.

events.text: {npc} kicks your bench as {he} passes it at {wd_inn}, and does not apologise. "Nice mask," {he} says. "Shame about whoever is wearing it." The hall goes quiet, waiting to see what kind of traveller you are.

effects.log: You laugh. It is the last thing {npc} expected, and {he} does not know what to do with it. {He} will remember that.

mem.note: was shamed in front of the shrine

effects.log: The bench catches {npc} behind the knees. The hall laughs. {npc} gets up red in the face and swears this is not over.

mem.note: gave you a name to remember

effects.log: "{npc}," {he} says. "Remember it." You will, as it turns out.

events.text: At {wd_inn} {npc} has beaten every guest at arm-wrestling over the offering table and is looking for someone new. {His} eyes find you. {He} sets an elbow on your table and smiles with too many teeth.

effects.log: It goes on a long time. You win, barely, and {npc} looks at you as if you had stolen something.
{npc} tells the hall you are afraid. Let {him}.

events.text: A blind temple-singer at {wd_inn} tells of a god who walked from the eastern domain to the western sea in a borrowed face and never once let the mask slip. The pilgrims argue over whether it is true. The singer only smiles and holds out a bowl.

choices.text: Put an offering in the bowl

effects.log: The singer tells you, privately, that the god slipped the mask exactly once, for a child.

choices.text: Tell a tale of your own

effects.log: Your tale is shorter and duller, but the hall is kind. The singer nods as if you had paid.

events.text: The host of {wd_inn} keeps a beam of marks: every pilgrim who sheltered a season has cut a small sign into the rafter above the hearth. Some are so old that the wood has grown over them. The host hands you the knife.

effects.log: You cut it small, in a corner, between two marks you do not know. It looks as if it has always been there.
You read them all. One of them makes you stop, for no reason you can name.

events.text: On the rafter above the hearth of {wd_inn}, among the marks of old pilgrims, someone long ago cut "{wd_past_title}". The host notices you staring. "A legend of this road," the host says. "They say whoever cut it will come back one day and settle the offering."

effects.log: You settle an offering two lifetimes old. The host laughs, then stops laughing, and takes it very carefully.

choices.text: Run your thumb over the mark

effects.log: The cuts fit your hand. Something in you settles, like a traveller setting down a pack.

events.text: The champion of {wd_inn} is a vast cheerful temple-cook who has never been beaten at the feast-bowl, and by the twelfth round the whole hall is standing on the benches. By the twentieth the cook is asleep on the flagstones and you are still upright, more or less, and the hall is chanting.

choices.text: Pour a libation for the cook

effects.log: You pour out a cup for the fallen champion. When the cook wakes, the first thing said is a laughing demand for a rematch next feast.
You walk out in a perfect straight line, and then sit down very carefully in the yard where nobody can see, and loosen your belt.

events.text: You remember the fourteenth round. After the fifteenth you lie down, only for a moment. You wake in the votive-store of {wd_inn} with a shrine goat looking at you and the house champion snoring among the candles, and someone has drawn a moustache on your mask in lamp-soot. You suspect the champion.

effects.log: The hall laughs with you, not at you, by the time you come back in. Mostly.
Fair is fair. The champion wakes, sees, and roars with laughter.

events.text: {npc} slams the bowl down across the table from you at {wd_inn}. "Again," {he} says, for the twentieth time. This time {his} chopsticks miss the dumpling. {npc} sits back, looks at the rafters, and slides gently under the table, still glaring.

mem.note: was helped up from under the table

effects.log: {npc} lets you, and hates it, and does not hate you quite as much as before.
The hall steps over {npc} all evening. {He} will remember every step.

events.text: "Under the table," {npc} says, very pleased, "is where you belong." You would argue, but you are under the table, too full to move, and the flagstones of {wd_inn} are warm and very comfortable, and {npc} is eating one more dumpling just to show it can be done.

effects.log: "Next feast," you say to the floor. {npc} laughs. It is almost friendly.
You swear it from the floor. {npc} eats to it.

events.text: The shrine's cantor at {wd_inn} sings first, a fast bright harvest hymn, and the hall claps. Then you sing, something slow that you did not know you remembered. When you stop, nobody claps for a moment. Then the cantor lowers the hymn-book and bows to you.

effects.log: You bow to each other. The cantor teaches you a new hymn as payment for the old one.
The two of you sing until dawn. The host gives you both free beds.

events.text: The cantor at {wd_inn} sings like water down a temple stair, and you sing like someone carrying it back up. The hall is polite about it, which is worse. Afterwards the cantor sits with you and shows you, kindly, where your breath went wrong.

effects.log: You learn more in an hour of losing than in a year of practice.

choices.text: Ask for a rematch next feast

effects.log: "Gladly," the cantor says. "Practise the third verse."

events.text: {npc} claims the first verse at {wd_inn}, chin high, voice ringing off the rafters, eyes never leaving your face. You do not match it. You answer under the breath, a single plain line, and the hall hushes to hear it, and {npc} finishes with a thin, furious smile.

effects.log: You sing a duet. {npc} sings it beautifully, and pretends not to have enjoyed it.

mem.note: lost the duel before a crowd

effects.log: You take the applause. {npc} takes the door.

events.text: At {wd_inn} the hall's praise goes to {npc}, and you are the first to bow, because the hymn was the better one and you knew it by the first verse. {npc} comes over, pink with pride. "Second place suits you," {he} says. "Come back when you are hungry."

effects.log: {npc} looks startled, and then nods once.
You practise all night in the votive-store. {npc} hears it, and smiles in the dark.

events.text: You and {npc} take a jar, three sticks of incense and a rice-cake from a stall, and go to the altar at the crossroads at sunset. Three bows to the sky, three to the earth. "Not born on the same day," {npc} says, "but on the same road." You say the rest of it together.

choices.text: Cut your palms and share the cup

mem.note: shared the cup of the oath

effects.log: A small cut, a shared cup. {npc} grins at you over the rim like someone who has finally come home.
"Whatever comes," you say. "Whatever comes," {npc} says back. It is enough.

events.text: {npc} kneels beside you at the crossroads altar and stops before the first bow. "They say you have done things," {he} says. "Hard things, the kind a god does. I do not care. I am not swearing to the stories. I am swearing to you." Then {he} bows.

mem.note: swore to you, not the stories

effects.log: You bow together, three and three. Whatever you are, you are no longer alone on the road.

choices.text: Tell {npc} the worst of it first

mem.note: heard the worst of you and swore anyway

effects.log: You tell {npc} the worst. {He} listens, and bows anyway.

events.text: {npc}, your sworn sibling, walks into the shrine yard with a cracked talisman and three tithe-collectors a day behind. "I would not ask," {npc} says, "but you would never forgive me if I did not."

effects.log: You meet the collectors at the shrine gate, together. They decide the tithe is not worth it.

choices.text: Hide {npc} and send the collectors astray

effects.log: You send the collectors three shrines the wrong way. {npc} sleeps in your loft and laughs about it for years.
You close the door. {npc} stands outside a long while before going. The road will hear of this.

events.text: A prayer-slip in {npc}'s untidy hand: "I am being bound at the new moon before the hearth-god. You are the only kin I have. If you are not there I will hold the rite open until you come, and everyone will be very annoyed with you."

choices.text: Walk all night to get there

effects.log: You arrive at dawn, dusty and late. {npc} throws both arms around you in front of the whole congregation.

choices.text: Send an offering and your regrets

effects.log: The offering arrives. {npc} writes back a short, polite slip. It is the politeness that stings.

events.text: {npc}, your sworn sibling, finds you at a wayside altar with a jar of good offering-wine and no reason at all. "The anniversary," {npc} says. "Of the crossroads. Or near enough. I lost count." You sit by the altar until the stars come out, and talk about nothing and everything.

choices.text: Raise a cup to the oath

effects.log: You raise your cup to the crossroads, and to the road, and to whoever is still to come.
You hear everything, the good years and the bad. {npc} has been waiting to tell someone.

events.text: You lay {wd_sworn} to rest at the foot of a crossroads shrine, because that is where the oath was sworn and where {wd_sworn} would have laughed to be remembered. You pour out a cup for the earth and one for the sky. The road is very quiet.

choices.text: Carve the oath on the stone

effects.log: You carve the words you said together. Pilgrims stop to read them for years.
You walk on, because that is what the road is for. You leave the cup on the stone.

events.text: {npc} is waiting on the old stone bridge between two domains, hand on a hilt. "Every shrine on this road tells your stories now," {he} says. "I am sick of them. Today the story ends."

ok.log: You beat {npc} on the worn stones, and help {him} up afterwards. {He} does not thank you.

fail.log: {npc} beats you on the worn stones and walks away without a word, which is somehow worse.

effects.log: {npc} stares at you. Then, slowly, {he} lowers the hand from the hilt. "One meal," {he} says. It turns into a long night, and a friendship.

events.text: {npc} sends a prayer-slip instead of a challenge this time. "I am tired of hating you," it says. "It takes too much effort and the stories keep getting better for you. Meet me at the waystation. I will pay."

effects.log: {npc} pays, as promised, and grumbles about it all night. By morning you are friends, more or less.

choices.text: Write back that you are busy

effects.log: {npc} reads the reply and tears it into very small pieces.

events.text: {npc}, whom you met at a wayside shrine and have not been able to stop thinking about, turns up at your door with two bowls of noodles and no excuse at all. "I was passing," {he} says. You live nowhere near anywhere.

effects.log: {npc} stays the season. By the end of it neither of you pretends it was a coincidence.
You eat together as friends. {npc} is a good friend. The look {he} gives you at the door says {he} hoped for more.

events.text: A prayer-slip comes from {npc}, whom you met on the road of the shrines: three pages about rivers and hostels and a goat {he} met, and at the very end, one line. "I keep wishing you were there to see it."

effects.log: You walk for a week. {npc} is standing at the river when you arrive, as if {he} knew.
You write back about your own rivers. The slips go on for years, warm and careful.

events.text: A temple-singer at a crossroads shrine tells of {wd_title}, who out-drank a cook, a champion and a sworn rival in a single feast season and never once spilled a drop. You sit at the back, masked. Nobody knows you. The tale is wildly wrong, and you are, it seems, a legend.

effects.log: It is not the name you were born with. It may be the one you are remembered by.
You laugh, and the road laughs with you, and the name follows you anyway.

events.text: You hear your own hymn hummed by a farmer in a vale you have never walked. The farmer learnt it from a pedlar, who had it from {wd_title}, who could, the pedlar swore, make a stone shrine weep with three notes.

effects.log: It is not the name you were born with. It may be the one you are remembered by.
You laugh, and the road laughs with you, and the name follows you anyway.

events.text: At a hostel far from any domain, a young pilgrim asks the host to point out {wd_title}. "The one whose sworn kin would cross a province for a prayer-slip," the pilgrim says. The host points at you.

effects.log: It is not the name you were born with. It may be the one you are remembered by.
You laugh, and the road laughs with you, and the name follows you anyway.

events.text: The children of a roadside village have a new game: one plays the tithe-collector, one the host, and one, always the smallest, plays {wd_title}, who comes in out of the rain and sets things right.

effects.log: It is not the name you were born with. It may be the one you are remembered by.
You laugh, and the road laughs with you, and the name follows you anyway.

events.text: Shrine-hosts on three roads have started bolting their offering tables to the floor. Nobody says why. Everybody knows why. They are waiting for {wd_title}.

effects.log: It is not the name you were born with. It may be the one you are remembered by.
You laugh, and the road laughs with you, and the name follows you anyway.

events.text: A pedlar looks at your sandals and your mask and laughs. "I know you," the pedlar says. "Every shrine from the eastern domain to the western sea knows you. {wd_title}, they call you. Is there a road you have not walked?"

effects.log: It is not the name you were born with. It may be the one you are remembered by.
You laugh, and the road laughs with you, and the name follows you anyway.
